summary:
Mission Control – Interactive Space Mission Simulator

Mission Control is an interactive educational space mission simulator designed to make space engineering more engaging and understandable. We developed a web-based application that allows users to design their own spacecraft, select mission destinations, choose scientific instruments and propulsion systems, and manage resources such as fuel, power, mass, and budget. The simulator evaluates the spacecraft design based on engineering constraints and allows users to launch missions and handle unexpected challenges during space operations. It also provides mission performance scores and a final mission report. This project addresses the challenge of understanding complex space engineering concepts through a practical and interactive learning experience. It is important because it encourages scientific curiosity, problem-solving, critical thinking, and awareness of the engineering decisions involved in real space exploration.
details:
Project Details – Mission Control: Interactive Space Mission Simulator

Mission Control is a web-based interactive simulator that allows users to experience the process of planning, designing, launching, and managing a space mission. Users can select mission objectives and destinations, choose spacecraft instruments, propulsion systems, launch vehicles, and communication systems, and adjust solar power capacity, fuel allocation, and mission budgets.

The application calculates important engineering parameters such as spacecraft mass, power requirements, available delta-v (Δv), and estimated mission cost. It checks whether the spacecraft meets essential engineering constraints before allowing launch. During mission operations, users face simulated challenges such as radiation storms, solar array contamination, and communication issues, where they must make decisions to maintain spacecraft performance.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, without requiring additional hardware or a database. The creative aspect is its combination of engineering calculations, resource management, and interactive decision-making in a single platform. Key factors considered include mass limitations, power consumption, propulsion efficiency, budget constraints, and spacecraft health.

The project’s intended impact is to make space engineering concepts easier to understand while encouraging critical thinking, problem-solving, and interest in space exploration.
